title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Oil Wipes Out, Tech Rolls Over, Dow Rides the Rotation
conditions.summary: Stocks rallied early and faded as investors rotated out of tech; the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq 1.1% while the Dow gained 0.4%. Oil plunged about 7.5% on hopes for US-Iran diplomacy.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 closed at 7,541.40, down 0.51%; Nasdaq Composite at 25,164.32, down 1.07%.
Dow rose 0.41% to 51,983.98; Russell 2000 slipped 0.21% to 2,805.88.
Stocks rallied early (S&P up about 1% mid-morning, Nasdaq up as much as 1.4%) before fading to session lows near the close.
Money rotated out of tech and chips: technology was the weakest sector, down about 2.4% in the afternoon.
Consumer discretionary led, with financials, industrials and materials also higher; energy producers fell with oil.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: WTI crude fell about 7.6% to roughly $96 and Brent about 7.6% to near $105 on reports the US and Iran are seeking a diplomatic end to the war.
ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October versus 54.6 expected and 54.5 prior; prices paid eased to 75.2.
Construction spending fell 1.9% in September versus an expected 0.4% gain.
10-year Treasury yield dipped about 3.5 basis points to near 4.89%; gold rose 1.5% and the VIX jumped 8.9% to 21.15.
Fed funds futures leaned toward a December rate hike, according to market reports, after last week's FOMC hold at 3.75%-4.00%.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: IDXX (IDEXX Laboratories): +21.9% — Q3 revenue rose 10% and the company raised its 2026 outlook.
EVGO (EVgo): +46.8% — controlling holder LS Power proposed buying the remaining shares for $2.00 each.
PERI (Perion): +31.2% — agreed to be acquired by Affle for $11.70 a share in cash.
TEM (Tempus AI): +8.7% — Q3 revenue up 23% and a raised full-year forecast.
LITE (Lumentum): -18.6% — agreed to an all-stock acquisition by Marvell valued around $115 billion.
MRVL (Marvell Technology): -12.7% — the acquirer in the Lumentum deal.
ORCL (Oracle): about -8.5% — announced a $20 billion raise in stock and bonds, stoking AI funding worries.
KOS (Kosmos Energy): -13.5% — Q3 loss, lighter Q4 production guidance and a sliding oil price.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Apple (after close): revenue $114.48B vs $113.47B expected and EPS $2.10 vs $2.00; shares down about 1% after hours.
Palantir (after close): beat and raised guidance; shares down about 3% after hours.
IDEXX (before open): beat and raise sent shares up about 22%.
Check Point Software (before open): Q3 revenue fell 1% to $670M; stock closed down about 7%.
Kosmos Energy (before open): Q3 net loss and soft output guidance; stock down about 13.5%.

sections.title: Business News
items: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal, 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, expected to close in the first half of 2028.
Oracle launched a $20 billion capital raise split between new stock and investment-grade bonds to fund AI buildout.
Crypto exchange Binance was hit by a reported hack of about $6.3 billion, weighing on bitcoin.
Perion agreed to be acquired by Affle at a 34.5% premium, with a go-shop period through December 11.
Anheuser-Busch CEO Brendan Whitworth will leave at the end of November to lead Equinox.

sections.title: On Deck
items: US midterm elections take place Tuesday.
JOLTS job openings for September at 9:00 AM CT.
Before the open: Marathon Petroleum, Archer-Daniels-Midland, Sysco, Bunge and Energy Transfer.
After the close: AMD and Super Micro Computer.
Six Fed officials are scheduled to speak this week; October jobs report due Friday at 7:30 AM CT.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Monday, November second, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sliding into the water and the last set is rolling in. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon chasing sandpipers down the beach and he is still wagging. Give the crew a big hello, Gus! Here's the final set. The S and P 500 slipped about half a percent to seven thousand five hundred forty-one. The Nasdaq wiped out a little over one percent to twenty-five thousand one hundred sixty-four. But the Dow paddled the other way, up four tenths of a percent to fifty-one thousand nine hundred eighty-four. And it was a gnarly ride. Stocks rallied early, with the S and P up about one percent in the morning, then faded into the close. Money rotated out of tech and chips and into consumer names, financials and industrials. Technology was the worst sector, down more than two percent. Now the wind and weather. The big story was oil. Crude crashed about seven and a half percent to around ninety-six dollars, on reports the United States and Iran are looking for a diplomatic path to end the war in the Middle East. On the data side, the I S M manufacturing index rose to fifty-five point five, beating forecasts and showing the strongest factory growth in years. Construction spending fell almost two percent in September, though, when a small gain was expected. The ten year Treasury yield dipped about three basis points to near four point eight nine percent. Gold climbed one and a half percent, Bitcoin slipped about one percent, and the fear gauge, the VIX, jumped almost nine percent to twenty-one. Now the lineup. IDEXX Laboratories caught a monster wave, up nearly twenty-two percent after strong sales and a raised outlook. Gus, that one earned a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! E V go jumped forty-seven percent after its biggest owner offered to buy out the rest of the shares. On the wipeout side, Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum in an all stock deal valued around one hundred fifteen billion dollars. Lumentum fell about nineteen percent and Marvell sank about thirteen percent. Oracle dropped more than eight percent after announcing a twenty billion dollar capital raise, with worries about the cost of the A I build out. Check the tide chart. Apple reported after the bell and beat on both sales and profit, but the stock was down about one percent after hours. Palantir beat and raised its outlook, yet slipped about three percent late. Before the open, IDEXX hung ten, while Check Point Software fell about seven percent on a revenue dip. Beach talk. A reported six billion dollar hack at the crypto exchange Binance rattled digital assets. And Perion jumped thirty-one percent after agreeing to be bought by Affle. Tomorrow's forecast. It's Election Day, with the midterms on the ballot, so expect some wind. Job openings data drops at nine A M Central. Six Fed officials are scheduled to speak this week. Before the open we hear from Marathon Petroleum, Archer Daniels Midland and Sysco, and after the close it's A M D and Super Micro Computer. Want a read on a single wave? Type any stock, E T F or futures contract into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Wax your board, soul surfers, and catch the Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
